svg.title: DN 9 Poṭṭhapāda Sutta — Ultimate cessation of perception
svg.desc: A memory map of DN 9: mistaken accounts of cessation, training in which one perception replaces another through the jhānas to nothingness, perception preceding knowledge, perception not the self, undeclared views versus the four truths, ungrounded versus well-grounded teaching, and worldly conventions used without clinging.

g.text: How does perception reach its ultimate cessation?
Four ways people explain the ultimate cessation of perception
It comes and goes — and one is percipient or not
They draw perception in and draw it out
They draw perception in and draw it out
WITH CAUSE AND CONDITION · SAHETŪ SAPPACCAYĀ
“Through training, one perception arises; through training, one perception ceases.”
sikkhā ekā saññā uppajjati, sikkhā ekā saññā nirujjhati
One perception ceases; a subtler actual perception arises
sensual perception ceases → seclusion-born uplifting joy and pleasure arises
seclusion-born uplifting joy and pleasure ceases → collectedness-born uplifting joy and pleasure arises
collectedness-born uplifting joy and pleasure ceases → equanimous pleasure arises
perceptions of form, impact, and diversity cease → base of boundless space arises
rūpasaññā · paṭighasaññā · nānattasaññā nirujjhanti → ākāsānañcāyatanasukhumasaccasaññā uppajjati
base of boundless space ceases → base of boundless consciousness arises
base of boundless consciousness ceases → base of nothingness arises
“Intending is worse for me; not intending is better.”
cetayamānassa me pāpiyo, acetayamānassa me seyyo
Neither intends nor constructs → those perceptions cease → he touches cessation
na ceva ceteti, na ca abhisaṅkharoti · tā ceva saññā nirujjhanti · nirodhaṁ phusati
Thus, there is the gradual attainment of the ultimate cessation of perception while being clearly aware
PERCEPTION THEN KNOWLEDGE · SAÑÑĀ PACCHĀ ÑĀṆAṀ
Perception arises first; through its arising, knowledge arises
“It was dependent on this that knowledge arose in me.” · idappaccayā kira me ñāṇaṁ udapādi
PERCEPTION AND THE SELF · AÑÑĀ SAÑÑĀ AÑÑO ATTĀ
Even granting any of these three selves, perception is still another thing
While that self remains, different perceptions arise and cease — so perception is one thing, the self another
tiṭṭhateva sāyaṁ attā … aññā ca saññā uppajjanti, aññā ca saññā nirujjhanti
What is set aside, and what is taught because it leads to Nibbāna
hoti · na hoti · hoti ca na ca · neva na na
na atthasaṁhitaṁ na dhammasaṁhitaṁ · na nibbānāya saṁvattati
This is the arising of suffering
This is the end of suffering
The way of practice leading to the end of suffering
A claim about exclusive happiness after death, versus Dhamma for abandoning self-acquisition
ekantasukhī attā hoti arogo paraṁ maraṇā
experience it even for a night or a day
know the path and way of practice
At whatever time milk is present, it is reckoned only as milk — not as curd, butter, or ghee
so too with coarse, mind-made, and formless: only the acquisition present is reckoned
These are worldly designations, expressions, conventions, and descriptions
which the Tathāgata uses without clinging
lokasamaññā · lokanirutti · lokavohāra · lokapaññatti · yāhi tathāgato voharati aparāmasan
